hook_candidates.text: In 1925, an intact ship sailed alone with dinner still warm on the table.
Seventy-two seconds of signal changed how astronomers scanned the sky forever.
The radar alarm tripped at midnight, pointing toward an empty patch of ocean.
The deepest vault on Earth held fifty records, but zero visitors were allowed inside.
A three-man crew vanished from an island lighthouse without leaving a single trace.
Deep below the Mediterranean floor lies an intact temple no diver was meant to see.
Astronomers logged the exact frequency, yet forty-nine years later the source remains completely silent.
Over twenty miles of ancient stone sat buried beneath coastal sand for a millennium.

beats.text: In 1925, a con man sold the Eiffel Tower. Then he sold it again.
Victor Lustig read a newspaper editorial lamenting the steep maintenance costs of the Paris landmark.
He forged official Ministry stationery and invited the city's top scrap metal merchants to a secret meeting.
Lustig convinced them the city had decided to demolish the tower and sell seven thousand tons of steel.
Dealer Andre Poisson handed over seventy thousand dollars in cash and bribes to secure the contract.
Lustig immediately boarded a train to Vienna with a suitcase stuffed with French francs.
Poisson was too embarrassed to report the scam to police, so Lustig returned six months later to repeat it.
Decades later, Paris archives still preserve the con man who sold the Eiffel Tower.
